author: Ryan McHarg
purpose: AgentEchelon is a governed, multi-party, multi-channel AI platform you deploy into your own AWS account. This context lets the assistant answer questions about the platform itself - what it is, how it works, and where a topic is documented.
overview: AgentEchelon is a governed, multi-party agentic AI platform that runs in your own AWS account and serves internal and customer-facing use cases from one place. A core feature is that agent governance can be enforced with AWS's own identity primitives instead of a bolted-on policy engine. Every user, assistant, and conversation is an AWS resource with an ARN; every actor holds a bearer-pinned ident
answering_guidance: Answer from these summaries and, when deployed in Aurora mode, from the retrieved full docs. Point the user at the named doc path for detail. Do not fabricate; if it is not here, say so. The `author`, `since`, `license` and `repository` fields above answer questions about who made the platform and where its source is - answer those from here rather than from the deploying company's documents, which do not carry them. You cannot browse the web or read that repository: cite it as where the source lives, and do not offer to look anything up in it.

docs.title: Admin Console Guide
docs.summary: How operators use the AgentEchelon admin dashboard to check platform health, review how the assistants are performing, and administer conversations. Written to be portable - it describes behavior, not any specific AWS account.

docs.title: Bringing Your Own Admin Console and Admin Auth
docs.summary: This guide explains how to run AgentEchelon's operator surface - analytics, administration, evaluations, experiments - **behind your own application's admin console and admin authentication**, instead of the built-in console and the deployment's own Cognito groups.

docs.title: Aurora Mode Guide
docs.summary: AgentEchelon ships with two analytics backends. **Athena mode** (default) is serverless and cheap at low volume. **Aurora mode** adds a VPC with Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 for sub-second dashboard queries, multi-turn evaluation, drift detection, and cross-conversation context search.

docs.title: The Guest Issuer
docs.summary: How a deployment admits an anonymous visitor, what holds the visitor to their own conversation, how a visitor becomes a person, and how an operator runs it: the kill switch, the signing key's rotation and the alarms. This guide describes what is built.

docs.title: A/B Testing and Running Battles
docs.summary: How to run real A/B model experiments on your own traffic, measure which model wins, promote the winner, and use Battle Mode to put two assistants head to head on the same prompt.

docs.title: Image Generation Providers
docs.summary: **Audience:** Deployers configuring image generation. Image generation is a normal profile capability - an intent routed to an image model in a profile's `models.byIntent` (the `image_generation` intent as shipped) - and the image A/B experiments and battles are built on top of it. Anything that calls `invokeImageGenModel`.

docs.title: Model Strategy

docs.title: Performance optimization (reducing latency)
docs.summary: AgentEchelon ships with **cost-lean defaults**, not latency-optimized ones. Out of the box every request path is serverless and scales to zero: Lambdas are on-demand (no provisioned concurrency), Aurora runs at a 0.5 ACU minimum, RDS Proxy is off, and the intent classifier is a live model call. docs.title: Deploying the frontend (CloudFront + S3)
